newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds close weaker in active trading.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds close weaker in active trading.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed weaker in active trading on Tuesday, with the market largely mirroring losses recorded by U.S. Treasuries today and yesterday, when most Canadian fixed-income markets were closed.

"Most of it was just making up for the fact that we were closed yesterday. The U.S. bond market has got some negative sentiment running through it right now," said Rich Wylie, a fixed-income economist with TD Securities Inc.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.84 to C$120.13 to yield 6.467 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 6/32 to yield 6.49 percent. The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to two basis points from four basis points at Friday's close.

U.S. treasuries weakened on Monday when most Canadian market players were away because of the market and civic holiday in many provinces. While Canada may have appeared to do worse than the U.S. market in today's session, it was simply adding to the losses from Monday.
Analysts said trading was active in Canada due partly to the holiday, as many traders and investors squared up positions and porfolios after missing Monday's session.
Dealers said the focus for the rest of this week's trading was new supply in both countries.
"We've got the refunding that's coming up, so I think you're unlikely to see the market perform particularly well ahead of that," said TD's Wylie.
The U.S. Treasury will auction US$12 billion of 10-year notes on Wednesday and US$10 billion of 30-year notes on Thursday.
In Canada, the federal government on Wednesday will auction C$2.3 billion of bonds due June 1, 2008.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.44 to C$109.42 to yield 5.953 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond fell 3/32 to yield 6.24 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds widened to 29 basis points from 27 basis points at Friday's close.
